checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Compact conical tubing coiled into oval shape, noticeably shorter than a trumpet.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The instruments appear to be standard Bb trumpets or cornets with typical proportions, not the compact oval-coiled shape characteristic of pocket trumpets or specific cornet variants described as 'noticeably shorter'. The tubing layout is standard vertical loop, not a tight oval coil.
All five instruments have clearly flared bells pointing downwards/forwards relative to their upright stance.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tubing diameter gradually increases from mouthpiece to bell.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Visual inspection confirms the standard conical bore expansion from the leadpipe area down to the bell flare.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Three piston valves arranged vertically on top with finger buttons.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Each instrument clearly displays three vertical valve casings with finger buttons on the upper section.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Cup-shaped detachable mouthpiece inserted into leadpipe.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Silver-colored cup-shaped mouthpieces are visible inserted into the top of the leadpipes on all instruments.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Finger hooks and thumb ring present for grip.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Small finger hooks and rings are visible on the valve casing blocks and tuning slides, though slightly obscured by reflections.
The instruments exhibit a consistent golden-yellow lacquered brass finish with high reflectivity.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Valve casings are cylindrical with visible seam lines.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The valve casings are cylindrical; while seam lines are subtle due to the polish, the structural form is correct.
The bell rims show the characteristic thickened, rolled wire edge typical of brass instruments.

artifact_observations.location: Valve clusters and tubing intersections (middle instruments)
artifact_observations.reasoning: The mechanical complexity of the valve sections is simplified or melted. Tubing appears to fuse into the valve casings without clear separation or proper solder joints. Some valve buttons look like they are emerging directly from the tube walls rather than separate casings.

Reflections on the bells are somewhat generic and repetitive, lacking the specific environmental detail one might expect from such a highly polished surface, suggesting a texture mapping artifact common in AI generation.
The instruments appear to float slightly or merge with the black floor. There is no distinct shadow cast on the ground plane, making the spatial grounding ambiguous.
